tool_descriptions.bash: Run a shell command in the sandbox and return its standard output and standard error as one text. Put the command line in `sh`. Every call gets a new shell rooted at the working directory; chain steps that depend on each other with && inside a single command. There is no exit-code field: append `; echo "exit=$?"` when the status matters. Commands cannot read input, so pass non-interactive flags.
tool_descriptions.edit: Replace one exact piece of text in an existing file. `file` names the file, `find` is the current text, copied exactly with its whitespace and without line-number prefixes, and `replace` is the new text that takes its place. The current text must occur exactly once in the file. Read the file before editing it so the text matches what is on disk now.
tool_descriptions.glob: List the files whose paths match a glob pattern such as `**/*.py` or `src/**/*.md`. `name_glob` is the pattern; `under` is an optional directory to search, the working directory by default.
tool_descriptions.grep: Search file contents for a regular expression and return the matching lines with their file paths and line numbers. `regex` is the expression; `under` optionally limits the search to one directory and `file_glob` to file names matching a pattern such as `*.py`.
tool_descriptions.read: Read a file and return its lines with a line number in front of each, or list the entries of a directory. `file` names the file or directory. Up to 2000 lines are returned by default; use `from` (the first line, counting from 1) and `count` (the number of lines) to page through longer files. The line-number prefixes are not part of the file.
tool_descriptions.write: Write the complete content of a file; the file and any parent directories it needs are created, and an existing file is overwritten. `file` names the file and `text` is the full new text. Read an existing file before you replace it. To change only part of a file, use the edit tool instead.

edit./properties/file: Absolute path of the file to change.
edit./properties/find: Current text to be replaced, exactly as it appears in the file.
edit./properties/replace: The text to put in its place.

glob./properties/name_glob: Glob pattern to match, such as **/*.py.
glob./properties/under: Optional directory to search; the working directory by default.

grep./properties/under: Optional directory to search; the working directory by default.

read./properties/file: Absolute path of the file or directory to read.
read./properties/from: Optional first line to return, counting from 1.
read./properties/count: Optional number of lines to return.

write./properties/file: Absolute path of the file to write.
write./properties/text: The complete new content of the file.
